name: Sumner
headline: Sumner: a small valley city where SR 167 meets SR 410, with a Sounder station downtown.
lede: Sumner sits in the valley of north Pierce County, with Puyallup to the west, Auburn to the north and Bonney Lake up the hill to the east. This guide covers getting around, parks and trails, schools, everyday errands, housing and city plans, and what’s nearby, with a source for every fact.

notes: The Census Bureau’s QuickFacts page for Sumner could not be loaded this session. Housing and household figures come from the City’s statistics page, which labels them U.S. Census Bureau 2025 data, and from Census Reporter’s ACS 2024 5-year profile; the two agree on 4,586 households and a $519,900 median home value.

Commute time differs by source: Census Reporter gives a mean travel time to work of 29.6 minutes (ACS 2020–2024), while the City’s statistics page shows 30.2 minutes. This guide uses the Census Reporter figure.

Land area differs by source: Wikipedia’s infobox gives 7.53 square miles of land (7.65 total), its text gives 7.51 square miles of land, Census Reporter gives 7.6 square miles and the City says 7.2 square miles. The guide does not state an area.
The City lists a 2025 population of 10,871; Census Reporter gives 10,733 for 2020–2024. Both are estimates; the 2020 census count is 10,621.
Sumner’s exact incorporation date was not stated on any page read. The City’s walking tour says George Ryan became the first mayor in 1891 and that Sumner changed from a town to a city in 1928.

Garage timing has slipped: Sound Transit’s 2024 groundbreaking release and Wikipedia list completion in 2026, while Sound Transit’s project page now says it expects the garage to open to the public in late 2026 or early 2027. Stall counts also vary (600 in the release, 602 in other reports). Check Sound Transit before counting on garage parking.
School district size differs: the district reports 11,033 students for 2025–26, while Wikipedia gives 9,793 with no year. This guide uses the district’s figure.
Part of the Sumner Link Trail is closed for the White River Restoration project; the City expects it to fully reopen in the first quarter of 2027 or sooner.

The new Sumner Library has no opening date yet. The library system says construction will take about 22 to 24 months after the October 2025 groundbreaking, and one date on its page (site work beginning Oct. 19, 2026) looked inconsistent, so it is left out.
Rhubarb Days dates are for 2026 from the City’s event page; 2027 dates were not yet posted.

Some pages could not be read this session and were left out: the WSDOT SR 410 corridor sketch, the main Wikipedia pages for SR 167 and SR 410 (a Wikipedia mirror was used instead), and Pierce County’s Beyond the Borders page. Sounder travel times from Sumner were not stated on any page read.
The City’s 2021 handout on the SR 410/166th Avenue interchange described a planned fix, but its current status could not be confirmed, so it is left out.

chapters.title: Getting around and commutes
chapters.intro: The City describes Sumner as sitting at the junction of three state freeways, and Sounder trains stop downtown. Census figures put the mean travel time to work for Sumner residents at 29.6 minutes (2020–2024).
items: Sumner station at 810 Maple Street has 13 weekday Sounder S Line round trips, north to King Street Station in Seattle and south to Tacoma Dome or Lakewood. The permanent station opened March 10, 2001.
Before the garage, the station had 302 spaces in two lots, with an overflow lot on Academy Street that takes a paid reservation on weekdays. About 190 stalls were closed during construction.
Sound Transit broke ground on August 6, 2024 on a 600-stall garage, about 500 net new spaces, as part of a $49 million project.
Sound Transit’s project page says it expects the garage to open to the public in late 2026 or early 2027, with pedestrian and bicycle improvements included.
ST Express Route 578 runs all day from the station to Puyallup, Auburn, Federal Way and downtown Seattle. Peak-only Route 596 links the station with the Bonney Lake park and ride.

Pierce Transit local service ended when Sumner withdrew from the transit district in 2012. Beyond the Borders runs a free weekday fixed route for youth, disabled, senior and low-income residents, serving the YMCA, library, grocery stores and senior center.
Pierce County runs a weekday dial-a-ride service between the station, downtown Sumner and Bonney Lake, and a BusUp shuttle to industrial businesses began in January 2023.
SR 167 curves north along the Puyallup River through Sumner, with interchanges at SR 410 near the train station and at 24th Street East. Its HOT lanes begin in King County, not in Sumner.
A 107.44-mile highway that begins at SR 167 in Sumner and runs east through Bonney Lake, Buckley and Enumclaw, past Mount Rainier National Park and over Cayuse and Chinook passes to Naches.

chapters.title: Parks and outdoors
chapters.intro: Sumner’s city parks range from ball fields to a downtown plaza, and the paved Sumner Link Trail follows the White River and connects to regional trails.
items: 5.5 miles of paved trail along and across the White River, with picnic areas, workout facilities and trailheads. It links north to the Interurban and Lakeland Hills trails and south to the Foothills and Riverwalk trails.
The State Street trailhead at 13114 63rd St. E. has public parking and restrooms. The 16th Street and 24th Street turnarounds and the 142nd Loop have street parking only.

A City project to reduce flood risk and restore salmon habitat, reconnecting nearly 200 acres of floodplain to the White River. Phase 1 finished in October 2024; construction is scheduled to last until 2027.

The Link Trail through the restoration site is closed, and the trail no longer crosses the 24th Street bridge. The new trail will sit higher, on a forested berm, and is expected to fully reopen in the first quarter of 2027 or sooner.
At 5604 Graham Ave., with a main baseball field, two youth baseball fields, two soccer fields, volleyball, basketball and tennis courts, a jogging trail, a play area and a concession stand.
At 15603 Meade McCumber Road, with a covered, lighted court for basketball, pickleball and volleyball, an inclusive playground, a picnic shelter and barbecues.
At 1300 Park Street, with a playground, picnic tables, a basketball and pickleball court, horseshoe pits and a sports field.
At 1602 Bonney Ave., with basketball, soccer, a picnic area, a play area and a temporary pop-up dog park.
Reuben A. Knoblauch Heritage Park, at 914 Kincaid Ave., is a half-acre downtown plaza with tables, umbrellas and lighted seating. Later phases are not yet complete.

chapters.title: Schools
chapters.intro: Most of Sumner is in the Sumner–Bonney Lake School District, with some portions in the Dieringer and Puyallup school districts. Boundaries change; confirm school assignment with the district for any specific address.
items: Reported 11,033 students in 2025–26, with nine elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools. The district office is at 1202 Wood Avenue in Sumner.
The cities of Bonney Lake and Sumner, parts of Edgewood and Pacific, and unincorporated Pierce County, including most of Alderton and North Puyallup and portions of Lake Tapps and Tehaleh.
Middle schools are Lakeridge, Mountain View and Sumner; high schools are Bonney Lake High School and Sumner High School.
Bonney Lake, Crestwood, Daffodil Valley, Donald Eismann, Emerald Hills, Liberty Ridge, Maple Lawn, Tehaleh Heights and Victor Falls.
The City notes the district offers Career and Technical Education, DECA and International Baccalaureate programs.
The district’s website has boundary maps under Transportation and a boundary revisions page under Construction.
Local schools in Sumner, Puyallup and Orting take part in a lahar evacuation exercise; the 2026 drill was set for April 23, with rolling road closures on Valley Avenue, Main Street and 160th Street.

chapters.title: Everyday errands
chapters.intro: City Hall, the library and the Sounder station sit near downtown, and the City runs its own water and sewer utilities.
items: At 1104 Maple Street. The City lists Metro Animal Services for animal control and the City of Bonney Lake Recreation Program for recreation.

A Pierce County Library System branch. A new 17,500-square-foot library on East Main Street broke ground on October 2, 2025, replacing the 10,000-square-foot building, which stays open during construction.
The Sumner Police Department describes itself as an accredited law enforcement agency, with 24-hour dispatch through South Sound 911.
The City lists East Pierce Fire & Rescue as its fire service.
The City’s Public Works handles water and sewer, and Puget Sound Energy provides power and natural gas. Sumner Alert sends emergency and community alerts by address.
Sumner calls itself the “Rhubarb Pie Capital of the World.” In 2026 Rhubarb Days ran June 20 on downtown Main Street, with live music, food trucks, a kids’ zone and local vendors.
Sumner hosts part of the four-part Daffodil Parade each April, along with Tacoma, Puyallup and Orting.
REI has corporate offices and a large distribution center in Sumner, and Dillanos Coffee Roasters is based here.
The City describes the area its White River work protects from flooding as Pierce County’s largest manufacturing center, with 16,000 jobs.
The Fleischmann’s Yeast plant was completed in June 1913 and finished its final production in Sumner in 2023.

chapters.title: Housing and neighborhoods
chapters.intro: The City updated its Comprehensive Plan and Town Center Plan for 2026. Sumner lies in the Mount Rainier lahar hazard zone, so location matters.
items: Owner-occupied housing rate 54%, median owner-occupied home value $519,900 and median gross rent $1,974, from Census data quoted by the City.
4,586 households, with about 2.3 persons per household (Census, 2020–2024).
The City Council approved the 2025 Comprehensive Plan amendments on November 24, 2025; they took effect January 1, 2026.
The 2025 update lowered allowed building heights on parts of Main Street, Cherry Avenue and North Street from five to four stories and added an overlay zone along Zehnder Street and 57th Street East.
Ten parcels south of WinCo were rezoned to Medium Density Residential and four to Interchange Commercial, covering 19.9 acres in the southeast urban growth area.
About 5,600 years ago the Osceola Mudflow left deposits up to 300 feet thick over part of where the city now stands. Sumner, Orting and Puyallup lie in the lahar hazard zone for Mount Rainier.
A 2009 USGS study named Sumner among the communities with the highest percentages of people and assets in the Mount Rainier lahar hazard zone. Ask about any specific address.
Pierce County runs 42 outdoor warning sirens in the Puyallup and Nisqually river valleys, tested at noon on the first Monday of every month, and lists Sumner as a partner.
In 1926 the Ryan family gave land on Main Street to the city for a park. The house on the site, once a library, was found beyond repair and removed in 2025; the site is slated for future design.

chapters.title: What’s nearby
chapters.intro: Sumner sits where the Puyallup and White river valleys meet, between Puyallup, Auburn and Bonney Lake, with SR 410 leading toward Mount Rainier.
items: West of Sumner, with 42,973 people at the 2020 census. It is home to the Washington State Fair, which draws over a million visitors a year.
To the east, with 22,487 people at the 2020 census. It incorporated as a town on February 28, 1949, and SR 410 bisects the city.
An unincorporated community and census-designated place in Pierce County, with 12,962 people at the 2020 census.
West of Sumner, with 12,327 people at the 2020 census. It incorporated on February 28, 1996.
Mainly in King County, with 87,256 people in 2020. Sounder trains run from Auburn station to downtown Seattle in about 30 minutes.
SR 410 leads from Sumner through Enumclaw and Greenwater into Mount Rainier National Park, following the Chinook Scenic Byway from Enumclaw.
